[Date of appeal]

To: [Payer appeals department and mailing or electronic submission address]

Re: Appeal of adverse benefit determination  
Member: Emerson Iverson  
Member ID: W898477218  
Reference number: POC-007830134D-50943  
Requested procedure: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial notice: August 3, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The clinical record directly establishes the opposite: the MRI demonstrates a surgically treatable lesion that corresponds to the patient’s symptoms, examination findings, and functional impairment.

The May 26, 2026 lumbar MRI shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is a specific anatomic abnormality at the level corresponding to the patient’s right-sided radicular symptoms. The patient has pain radiating into the right calf, a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, and positive provocative testing on the affected side. The patient also cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. These findings provide clinical and radiographic correlation rather than an imaging finding without relevant symptoms.

The condition has persisted and progressively worsened for 18 months despite substantial conservative treatment. The patient completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility treatment, over 16 weeks from March 4, 2026 through June 24, 2026. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this course. The patient also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on April 4, 2026 provided only four weeks of partial relief. Continued conservative treatment has therefore not adequately controlled the patient’s symptoms or restored function.

The requested CPT 63030 procedure is directed at decompressing the affected nerve root and addressing the L4-L5 disc extrusion and severe lateral recess stenosis. The MRI, symptoms, examination, functional limitations, and failure of conservative treatment are mutually consistent and support the requested procedure.

The patient has no active infection, untreated substance use, or other documented factor that would explain the symptoms or make the requested treatment inappropriate. The patient is a nonsmoker and has a BMI of 29. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, is the treating surgeon requesting the procedure.

I request that the denial be reversed and that prior authorization for CPT 63030 be approved. If the denial is upheld, please provide the complete clinical-review rationale, identify the specific imaging information considered insufficient, and provide the exact medical-necessity policy or clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including its version and effective date. I have not quoted the plan’s policy because the policy document containing the criteria applied to CPT 63030 was not publicly available and was not included with the denial information.

Please consider all records submitted with the prior authorization request, including the May 26, 2026 MRI report, the physical therapy discharge note, treatment history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical documentation. Please send the appeal decision and any further hearing instructions in writing.

This appeal is submitted within the deadline stated in the denial notice, which identifies January 30, 2027 as the appeal deadline.

Sincerely,

Emerson Iverson  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]
